reporting_basis: SOLO / STANDALONE. Determined 2026-08-26. Union Bank PLC has no subsidiary. The FY2023 annual report's Basel-III capital-adequacy disclosures (Section B/C, 'Quantitative Disclosure: as on 31.12.2023') present the required 'Solo' and 'Consolidated' columns side by side for every capital-adequacy line item (CET-1, Tier-1, Tier-2, RWA, CRAR, etc.); the 'Consolidated' column is blank/dash ('-') throughout, and the qualitative narrative states explicitly: 'Union Bank PLC. is maintaining Capital to Risk Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) at 11.11% on SOLO basis against the regulatory minimum level of 12.50%.' Every Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss Account across all 12 archived years (2013-2024) is headed simply 'Balance Sheet' / 'Profit and Loss Statement' with no 'Consolidated' qualifier, i.e. Solo is the bank's only reporting basis, not one of two.
notes: annual_reports/UNIONBANK archive covers 2013-2024 (12 text files, all sanity-checked as substantive, non-scanned extractions covering the full financial statements -- ranging 3,525 to 12,146 lines each). Union Bank PLC is a Shariah-based Islamic bank from inception (incorporated 07 March 2013): reports 'Investments' rather than conventional 'Loans and Advances', and 'Classified Investments' rather than 'NPL', consistent with EXIMBANK/FIRSTSBANK/GIB conventions already established in this dataset. The bank's own 'Financial Performance at a Glance' / 'Annexure B Financial Highlights' pages are ONLY ever a 2-year (current + prior) comparative in every report (never a genuine 5-year table despite the page sometimes being titled similarly to other banks' 5-year tables) -- so this dataset's full 12-year series was built by combining EVERY report's own 2-year window with its neighbours' overlapping comparative columns, cross-validating each figure at least twice. Two reports' decorative/highlights pages (FY2013's 'Financial Performance at a Glance'/'Details of Capital Fund', FY2015's same, and FY2016's and FY2013/2014's 'Annexure B Financial Highlights') extracted as badly garbled or entirely blank text in this archive despite the surrounding financial statements (Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Notes) extracting cleanly; for those years, figures were instead reconstructed directly from the clean Balance Sheet / Profit and Loss Account / Note 12.4 Capital Adequacy schedules, with row/label misalignment (FY2015) resolved by matching each row's prior-year comparative value against the adjacent report's own confirmed figures. FY2024's 'Annexure B Financial Highlights' page suffered the same OCR/extraction failure (numbers and labels fused/unreadable) -- the same category of fault documented for FIRSTSBANK's FY2024 report by a concurrent session -- and was not used for any figure; FY2024's figures come entirely from its own (cleanly-extracted) Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Statement and Note 12.4. Every 'basis':'reported' figure in this dataset was cross-checked against at least one other report's comparative column (see each year's period_note for the specific match/divergence found). CRITICAL FINDING: Union Bank's FY2023 annual report was audited by M M Rahman & Co. and gave a CLEAN, UNQUALIFIED opinion, but Union Bank's FY2024 annual report -- audited a year later by a different firm (Syful Shamsul Alam & Co.), which gave a QUALIFIED opinion citing manipulated classified-investment system reports and improperly recognised income (per Bangladesh Bank letter DBI-7/4(4)/2025-347 dated 29 April 2025) -- shows a completely different FY2023 position in its own comparative column (equity BDT 11,884.45m not 16,337.89m; CRAR -18.81% not +11.11%; a BDT -2,875.22m loss not a BDT +1,607.89m profit; classified investments BDT 106,510.90m / 41.66% of gross investments, not BDT 9,263.05m / 3.62%). Per this dataset's standing methodology, the ORIGINAL/contemporaneous FY2023 figures are stored as the dataset's FY2023 values (the report is not internally arithmetically impossible, it was the underlying data that was later found to have been manipulated) -- see the 2023 entry below and 2023_Q4.json's period_note for the full finding, independently corroborated by contemporaneous Bangladesh press coverage (The Business Standard, The Daily Star) found via web research. FY2024 is a catastrophic terminal year: net loss BDT -257,936.69m (independently corroborated by The Daily Star's reported 'Tk 25,790cr', the largest annual loss in Bangladeshi banking history), shareholders' equity BDT -246,052.24m, CRAR -405.31%, classified investments 95.34% of gross investments, and a 74.20%-of-portfolio single-borrower-group concentration flagged in the Qualified Audit Opinion. Union Bank was declared 'non-viable' by Bangladesh Bank effective 5 November 2025 (Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025, Section 15), DSE trading was suspended the same date, and the bank was merged -- together with EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank and Social Islami Bank -- into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, under the same Bangladesh Bank resolution program documented independently by the concurrent sessions working EXIMBANK, GIB and FIRSTSBANK in this dataset; no standalone FY2025 report exists or is expected (see the FY2025 entry below). Only Q4/year-end (audited) data was extracted for any year; Q1/H1/Q3 unaudited interim data was not researched.

sources.notes: No FY2025 (year ended 31 December 2025) annual report or audited financial statement exists for Union Bank PLC as a standalone entity, and this is very likely a PERMANENT series-end, not a routine reporting lag. This dataset's FY2024 report (unionbank-annual-report-2024.txt, signed 13 November 2025) already discloses, in its own going-concern paragraph, that 'on October 9, 2025, the Advisory Council of the Interim Government of Bangladesh approved the merger of this bank with other four banks, under the direction of Bangladesh Bank, to form a new state-owned Islamic bank' -- i.e. the merger was approved before FY2025 (Jan-Dec 2025) had even closed, and the FY2024 report itself was signed under active administration (see the 2024 entry above). Independently confirmed via a time-boxed check on 2026-08-26, per this dataset's standing approach for banks in this same resolution program (see FIRSTSBANK, GIB): (1) a Wayback Machine CDX API pass over unionbank.com.bd's reports paths found the bank's site has PDFs only through 'financial-statement-24.pdf' (the FY2024 statement, crawled 2025-12-27, matching the FY2024 report already in this archive) and a generic, persistently-named 'ubl-annual-report.pdf' whose crawled content (checked directly, downloaded and inspected via pdfinfo/pdftotext, then deleted per project policy) turned out to be a stale, unrefreshed copy of the FY2021 annual report (Adobe InDesign creation date June 2022) rather than a new FY2025 filing -- no FY2025-named file exists in the CDX index at all; (2) a live fetch of unionbank.com.bd shows the site still branded 'Union Bank PLC' with normal-looking recent activity (a '185th board meeting, November 2025') but ALSO shows its logo linking to 'sammilitobankbd.com' and some internal URLs/page titles already referencing 'Sammilito Islami Bank PLC', i.e. the merger is already bleeding into the live site; (3) an attempted DSE (dsebd.org) company-page fetch was inconclusive (certificate/dynamic-content issues meant only a stale-looking 'Last AGM held on: 15-06-2023' was retrievable, itself consistent with a disrupted AGM cycle but not independently conclusive); (4) general web/news search independently and strongly corroborates the merger: Bangladesh Bank declared Union Bank 'non-viable' under Section 15 of the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025 effective 5 November 2025 and DSE suspended its share trading the same date (The Business Standard, 'Share trading of 5 troubled Islamic banks suspended before merger'), alongside EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank and Social Islami Bank; shareholders of all five banks will receive no shares in the merged entity because 'the value of assets tied to their existing shareholding is already negative' (The Daily Star); Union Bank entered the merger with (per a KPMG review) an NPL ratio of 97.8% as of September 2024 and a record FY2024 loss of 'Tk 25,790cr... the biggest loss in [Bangladesh] banking history' (The Daily Star) -- matching this dataset's own FY2024 figures closely; the five banks were merged into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC (Bangladesh Bank Letter of Intent issued 9 November 2025; a final operating licence reported granted in late 2025; Sammilito began a phased rollout of operations starting 2 December 2025 per some contemporaneous reports, with fuller integration by 18 August 2026 per this dataset's cross-bank research on the sibling banks EXIMBANK/GIB/FIRSTSBANK -- sources found in this session's research were not fully consistent on the exact 'independent operations' date, and this is recorded rather than adjudicated). Because the resolution/merger process was already underway before FY2025 even closed, and the bank was already operating under a Bangladesh-Bank-appointed Administrator by the time its (delayed, ~10.5-months-late) FY2024 report was even signed, there is no realistic expectation that a standalone FY2025 'Union Bank PLC' annual report will ever be filed; any FY2025-and-later reporting for this banking business would presumably surface, if at all, under 'Sammilito Islami Bank PLC' -- a distinct legal entity outside this dataset's scope. No 2025_Q4.json file was created for this bank.

sources.note: 9 files found and used, one per quarter: 2022 Q1 (https://unionbank.com.bd/assets/reports/half/Quarterly-Financial-Statement-as-on-31-March-2022.pdf), 2022 Q2/H1 (.../Half_Yearly_FS_2022_____.pdf), 2022 Q3 (.../Un-audited_Quarterly_Statement_Q3_as_on_30th_September,_2022.pdf), 2023 Q1 (.../1st-quarter-2023-ubl.pdf), 2023 Q2/H1 (.../2nd-q-ubl.pdf), 2023 Q3 (.../3rd_Quarter_Financial_Statement_as_on_30_September_2023.pdf), 2024 Q1 (.../31_March_2024.pdf), 2024 Q2/H1 (.../FS_30-06-2024.pdf), 2024 Q3 (.../Accounts.pdf, titled 'Quarterly Financial Statement as on 30 September 2024' on the listing page). 2022 Q1 and 2023 Q1 were genuine text-layer PDFs, extracted cleanly with pdftotext -layout. The other 7 were SCANNED IMAGE PDFs (2022 Q3 had zero usable embedded text; the other 6 had a badly corrupted/broken-font-encoding text layer that scrambled digits) -- all 7 were independently OCR'd (pdftoppm 300dpi + tesseract); every OCR'd figure's internal arithmetic (balance-sheet identity; Total Operating Income - Expenses = Operating Profit; - Provisions = PBT; - Tax = PAT) reconciles EXACTLY to the Taka for all 9 quarters, and every quarter's own prior-year comparative column was independently cross-checked against this dataset's corresponding quarter file where both exist (all matches, no discrepancies) -- strong corroboration that the OCR is reliable. A handful of individual P&L sub-lines ('Investments Income' gross and 'Profit Paid on Deposits', i.e. the pre-netting interest-income/interest-expense-equivalent figures) were illegible in specific quarters' own OCR; where recoverable, they were cross-referenced from an adjacent quarter's own comparative column (2022 Q2, 2023 Q3) or derived by subtraction from other confirmed figures (calculated_from_pl_components) -- flagged per-line-item in each quarterly/*.json file's basis field; never fabricated. PDFs deleted after extraction per project policy; the extracted/OCR'd text is retained at annual_reports/UNIONBANK/unionbank-unaudited-<year>-q<n>.txt for all 9 quarters. CRITICAL CROSS-VALIDATION FINDING (see insights.json for the full narrative): every 2024 Q1/Q2/Q3 filing's own 'December 2023' comparative column reproduces this dataset's stored ORIGINAL/contemporaneous FY2023 figures (Total Equity 16,337,889,333; Total Assets 295,347,564,528) EXACTLY, not the later-restated figures -- direct, dated proof that Union Bank's own books had not yet been restated as late as the Q3 2024 filing date (31 October 2024), six months before Bangladesh Bank's manipulated-data finding letter (29 April 2025). The Q1/Q2 2024 filings show continued normal, healthy, growing figures with no visible warning sign; Q3 2024 (30 September 2024) is the first quarter in the whole series to show a discrete quarterly LOSS (-801.81m), a quarter-on-quarter equity decline, and a sharp spike in classified-investment provisioning (1,040.0m for the quarter alone, vs a 100-460m range in every prior quarter) -- a real but comparatively modest crack, utterly dwarfed by the scale of what followed: combining this filing's 9-month cumulative figures with this dataset's existing 2024_Q4.json shows the IMPLIED Q4-2024-ALONE net loss was approximately -258,084.35m (BDT million) and Q4-2024-ALONE provisioning was approximately 237,333.96m (roughly 153x the entire first nine months combined) -- i.e. essentially the entire Bangladesh-record-setting FY2024 collapse was recognised in a single quarter (Q4, Oct-Dec 2024) at year-end audit, not gradually through the year's interim filings. None of the Q1-Q3 filings for any year (2022-2024) disclose classified investments, NPL ratio, or CRAR/capital-adequacy figures -- these condensed interim statements only cover the Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Cash Flow Statement, Statement of Changes in Equity, and a handful of selective notes (provisions-by-category, taxation, NAV/EPS); Basel-III capital disclosures appear only in the audited Annual Report.

sources.period: 2013-2021 Q1/Q2/Q3 (unaudited interim) -- INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-28, still not found
sources.notes: A follow-up session re-checked this gap from scratch with a broader method than the prior sweep: pulled the Wayback CDX API for the ENTIRE unionbank.com.bd domain with no keyword filter (3,630 total captures) and manually reviewed every one of the 127 PDF captures timestamped before 2022-01-21 (five days before the bank's DSE listing). Every pre-listing PDF is either an annual document ('financial_statements_for_the_year_of_31_december_20XX.pdf' for 2013-2019, annual-report PDFs, or annual Basel-II/III risk-based-capital disclosure PDFs) or unrelated (branch openings, forms, career postings, CSR/PR notices) -- zero quarterly, half-yearly, or condensed interim statements of any kind appear anywhere in the domain's pre-2022 crawl, under any path, not just the /assets/reports/half/ and /quarterly-statement paths the prior session already checked. Also newly checked a /assets/reports/psinformation/ folder (DSE-mandated Price Sensitive Information / disclosure notices, several titled '...Quarterly_Un-Audited_FS...') that the prior sweep's keyword filter had missed: its own earliest Wayback capture of any file is 2022-08-17 ('PSI_and_Disclosure_of_Quarterly_Un-Audited_FS1.pdf') -- i.e. this disclosure channel itself only starts appearing about 7 months after the bank's January-2022 listing, further corroborating (not contradicting) the 'no public quarterly-disclosure obligation before listing' explanation already on record. Net result: this independently reconfirms, via a materially broader full-domain sweep, the prior session's conclusion -- 2013-2021 Q1/Q2/Q3 unaudited interim statements were very likely never published for public consumption. Structurally analogous to this dataset's NRBBANK finding (no BSEC obligation before its own IPO). Separately noted here for a FUTURE session, and explicitly NOT pursued in this one (out of scope -- this task was instructed not to chase FY2025 data given the Sammilito Islami Bank merger series-end): a Wayback capture (first seen 2025-07-23) of https://unionbank.com.bd/news/half-yearly-business-conference-2025-of-union-bank-plc shows the bank held a 'Half Yearly Business Conference 2025', implying a H1-2025 (Jan-Jun 2025) unaudited interim statement may have been prepared internally even after FY2024's catastrophic collapse and before the 9-Oct-2025 merger approval / 5-Nov-2025 non-viable declaration. This does not change this dataset's FY2024 series-end determination (equity was already -246,052.24m and the bank was already under Bangladesh Bank administration by the time the delayed FY2024 audit was signed), but is flagged in case a future session's scope ever extends to FY2025.
